author: D. N. Kessler
title: Senator Bill Cassidy addresses judicial appointments, Iran operation concerns, and Pell Grant expansion
text:
U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D., posted a series of updates on his official X account between May 19 and May 20, 2026, addressing judicial appointments in Louisiana, concerns about military operations abroad, and changes to Pell Grant eligibility.
On May 19, Cassidy acknowledged recent federal confirmations in Louisiana: “Congratulations to Zachary Keller and judge Brian Barber on their confirmations as U.S. Attorney and U.S. Marshall for the Western District of Louisiana. They will serve Louisiana well.”
Later that day, Cassidy commented on ongoing military operations targeting Iran’s nuclear program: “While I support the administration’s efforts to dismantle Iran’s nuclear program, the White House and Pentagon have left Congress in the dark on Operation Epic Fury. In Louisiana, I’ve heard from people, including President Trump’s supporters, who are concerned about this war.” The senator highlighted concerns among his constituents regarding transparency around Operation Epic Fury.
On May 20, Cassidy turned attention to education policy: “Soon, Pell Grants can help students afford training for in-demand careers, giving Americans another path to a good-paying job and to the American Dream!”
Senator Cassidy serves on several key Senate committees—Finance; Energy and Natural Resources; and Veterans Affairs—as noted by his official website . He is known for co-founding the Greater Baton Rouge Community Clinic to provide free health and dental care to uninsured workers. Cassidy has also advanced policies focused on lowering healthcare costs and supporting coastal restoration initiatives.
A physician by training with degrees from Louisiana State University, Cassidy lives with his wife—a retired breast cancer surgeon—and their family in Louisiana.
